say: On November 14th, SpaceX's tower caught a Starship back from orbit.
Braking on engines alone would need about seven kilos of fuel per kilo of ship.
So the air does the braking: it falls on its belly, heat shield forward.
Then it flips upright and lights its engines.
The arms close on two pins that stick out about a foot.
So coming home is a heat problem: the shield must survive every trip.
Follow Media Diet for the physics behind the headlines.
